best_for: Home-media collectors and video hobbyists who need to merge, split or fix tracks, subtitles and chapters in MKV files, on Windows, Mac or Linux.

points.title: A toolkit for Matroska files
points.text: MKVToolNix creates, edits and inspects MKV files. mkvmerge builds MKV files from other media, mkvinfo shows what is inside, and mkvextract pulls tracks back out. A GUI ties the tools together for people who prefer not to use the command line.

points.title: Free, with a paid Store option
points.text: The tools are GPL v2 and free from the project site; the author takes donations through PayPal. A paid Microsoft Store edition exists for those who want the GUI with automatic updates, but it is not required.

points.title: Windows 10 and up, 32-bit still offered
points.text: Current builds support Windows 10 or Windows Server 2016 and newer. There is an installer and a portable archive, each in 64-bit and 32-bit. The installers listed here install machine-wide.

points.title: Macs need Ventura
points.text: Current Mac builds need macOS 13 or newer, in Intel and Apple silicon versions. Builds from v98 onward are made by a contributor, Graham Thompson. Older releases support older macOS, for example v54 for 10.15.

points.title: Linux is well covered
points.text: The Flatpak is published by the author, Moritz Bunkus, and Flathub marks it verified, for x64 and Arm64. There is also an AppImage needing glibc 2.28 or later, and repositories for Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora, AlmaLinux and more. Ubuntu 22.04 stops at v88.

points.title: History kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 56 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source, such as the older builds on the author's site.
